body:
Following the syntax suggested, created unique ID column as suggested to reduce unnecessary space. See:
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Ic8Bds9LzVr-lA9txKhfyjd5jDL-xPuQ/edit#gid=117802200&range=Q2

Also added leading 0's where sections extend into more than 1 digit.

These changes allow a choice to reduce width/noise and improve sorting for those using plain tables (expediting improvements) with 1 column. May also provide for automating future tool updates.

comments.body:
I'm not fan of making requirement id's longer just because it theoretically solves someones sorting problem.

Proposal to leave it as it is right now.

"Sorting problem" is a bit simplistic. The Unique ID's are central to meta database management tech, interoperability, and smoother future record updates. They do not need ro replace what you have. But appended to the end of the row will provide important manageablity. Thank you for your consideration.

Kimberley

ASVS data itself should be as clean as it can. If we could provide 2 different column for the same data (identifier), it could cause confusion.

We provide output in different format, including CSV and JSON. It's not too complicated to have one extra step before importing data to your own storage and add there own columns with data and formats needed.

Please note that your own guide notes these unique identifiers are coming
for manageability. Why make everyone build manually what what most will
need to ease adoption of the next set of changes? To expedite adoption and
mature the manageability of the standard, this is a win-win, and I was glad
to volunteer my time to help the industry spend their time improving apps
rather than the ASVS tool.

Hi @1songb1rd, thanks for your suggestion. I can see how this would be useful for various use-cases. As @elarlang noted, I think the best place to actually carry it out would be in the code which generates the various output formats (CSV, JSON, etc) rather than on the face of the standard itself.

Regarding the leading zeros issue, that was not something that was originally considered but now that you point it out I can see how that would have an impact on sorting. Leading zeros are not defined in the "How To Reference ASVS Requirements" section so I am not sure if we can adopt that immediately although I would be tempted to try and adopt it for the future.

So that we can understand the details slightly more:

* Which output format are you currently using, the CSV file?
* Can you live without the leading zeros?

Output formal: Most of the industry uses Excel spreadsheets, converting
from csv, txt, or anything they can get.

Living: I already did the work necessary and contributed it. I personally
need no additional effort to be expended on my behalf. I did the work
thinking of others - because IT security is already hard enough.

Requirements will be forwarded. People will start trying to sort the
information by sections, delegating work, and comparing the differences to
what they are already doing...that's when the challenges will begin. While
being user-friendly is certainly not required, it does help widen the user
base.

ASVS could more easily become related to OSCAL, CSA CMM, and NIST - for
example.
